subject: Acadia consolidation quote & technical fit
messages:
From: David L. Chen <david.chen@acadia.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acadia.com
Date: 2028-03-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFP: consolidation quote + parity ask

Olga —

Thanks again for the intro call this morning. Acadia is consolidating three inference vendors across ML infra, embeddings, and a small private deployment for regulated workloads. We need a concise response to the RFP attached (Acadia_RFP_v3.pdf) by EOD Friday. Key asks:

- Price parity vs incumbent (we’ll share redacted current rates in the RFP) — Acadia expects a matched unit cost or equivalent onboarding credits.
- Packaging: we currently pay a mix of seat licenses for orchestration and per-token for inference. Need guidance on seat vs consumption tradeoffs.
- Private deployment: one VPC + optional air-gapped plan for a regulated line of business (PHI).
- Migration support & credits; a short canary window & rollback protections.

Can you confirm you can provide a single consolidated quote that includes both hosted and private options, and highlight any technical caveats for runtime compatibility?

Appreciate a quick and pragmatic reply — we’re working toward a mid-April decision.

—David
Procurement, Acadia Systems
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: David L. Chen <david.chen@acadia.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-18T12:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: consolidation quote + parity ask

David —

Received, and thanks for the clear asks + RFP. High level response up front: we can produce a consolidated offer that targets price parity via a combination of committed consumption discounts, migration/onboarding credit, and optional seat-based management licenses for your SRE/ML platform teams. We can also support the private deployment you described (VPC + air-gap option), but the economics differ vs hosted.

Action items we’ll send by Friday:
- A consolidated commercial sheet with seat+consumption scenarios and a recommended baseline (see attached Acadia_Redwood_Initial_Econ.xlsx).
- Technical appendix describing runtime parity assumptions (model variants, quantization tolerances, KV cache behavior).
- Proposed migration credit schedule and recommended canary plan (30-day canary with traffic split and rollback clauses).

Couple of clarifying questions to sharpen the quote:
1) For the regulated workload, will Acadia require customer-managed HSM/KMS on day one, or is a managed KMS acceptable during pilot?
2) Do you have a target latency SLO for the private deployment (p50/p95 numbers) we should engineer to?

Looping in Jordan (legal) to make sure our standard canary/fallback language aligns with Acadia procurement expectations. I’ll also have Marcus put together the baseline discount math for seat vs consumption variants.

Thanks — olga
Olga Petrov
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-19T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Acadia consolidation quote & technical fit — discount structure + tech notes

Olga / Jordan —

Working notes for the Acadia econ sheet:

Commercial options (ballpark):
- Option A (Consumption-first): 20% committed discount on top of list per-token; additional 10% off if commit >= $250k/mo. Migration credit: 2 months of committed spend as onboarding credit.
- Option B (Seat + Consumption hybrid): fixed seat fee ($10k/mo per 10 management seats) + reduced per-token rate (35% off list for committed spend). Migration credit: 1 month seat + 1 month token credit.
- Option C (Dedicated pool): reserved capacity pricing (monthly commit) with throughput SLAs — best for predictable high-throughput workloads; includes priority scaling & custom quantization support.

Technical caveats / integration points:
- Runtime parity: open models will run identically; for custom or heavily quantized models we recommend a preflight compatibility window. Some model checkpoints require per-layer kernel adjustments for lower-bit quantization.
- KV cache: If Acadia relies on long context KV caching for chat-like flows, the dedicated pool reduces cold-start token cost. Consumption pricing needs to account for warmed prefix reuse.
- Private deployment: HSM/KMS integration is available; air-gapped installs require an SOW for software escrow + separate support plan.

Attachments: Dedicated_Pool_Sizing.pdf (size and GPU mix), Acadia_Redwood_Initial_Econ.xlsx (draft numbers).

I’ll convert these into the clean commercial sheet for Friday.
—Marcus
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: David L. Chen <david.chen@acadia.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acadia.com, samantha.ruiz@acadia.com
Date: 2028-03-20T11:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acadia consolidation quote & technical fit — discount structure + tech notes

Olga / Marcus —

Appreciate the draft options. A few immediate items from Acadia procurement and infra:

- Price parity: our incumbent is offering a blended effective rate (seat+token) that equates to roughly $0.0016 per token for our current mix. To move forward with Redwood we need either matching unit economics or a migration credit sufficiently large to offset the first 6 months' delta.
- Migration credits: we prefer a structure that front-loads credits against ingestion costs (first 60 days) and includes documented rollback / data egress assistance.
- Canary window: 30 days is acceptable, but we need a defined performance remediation SLA — e.g., p95 latency above X ms triggers a rollback or vendor remediation plan.
- Security evidence: please provide SOC2 Type II attestation and a short summary of your private deployment audit controls.

Also, for the seat vs consumption question: our platform team is open to a small admin seat pool if you can show the per-seat license reduces operational friction (single sign-on, RBAC for vector DB connectors) — otherwise we'd prefer consumption-only.

Can you provide a final consolidated quote (single page summary + line-items) and a short SOW draft that includes migration credits and operations acceptance criteria?

—David
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: David L. Chen <david.chen@acadia.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-22T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acadia consolidation quote & technical fit — consolidated offer

David —

Thanks — attached is our consolidated one-page summary and the draft SOW (SOW-Acadia-Redwood-2028.docx). High-level offer:

- Targeted parity structure: Redwood will match the incumbent blended effective rate for the first 6 months via a combination of a 22% committed-consumption discount + a migration credit equal to two months of your average spend (applied to token ingestion). If we can agree to a 12-month minimum commit, we can extend the discount floor to 28% after month-6.
- Seat option: optional admin seat pool ($9k/mo per 10 seats) — includes SSO, RBAC, and premium on-call for your SREs. If you take the seat pool, we can increase the first-6-month migration credit by 25%.
- Private deployment: offered as a VPC-managed plan with optional air-gap addon; private requires a distinct support addendum and one-time deployment fee (itemized in the SOW). HSM/KMS can be customer-managed; we documented the integration approach in the technical appendix.
- Canary and rollback: 30-day canary, with defined remediation SLAs in the SOW (p95 remediation target, rollback assistance and data egress support).

Next steps I propose:
1) Monica to run through onboarding and estimated runbook (I’ve looped her in).
2) Jordan to coordinate standard SOW redlines / procurement items.
3) If Acadia is comfortable, we will prepare a DocuSign packet with the one-page commercial + SOW and target a signing window the week of 3/27.

DocuSign draft and SOW link: https://app.redwood.com/deals/ACD-2028-07
Attachments: SOW-Acadia-Redwood-2028.docx

If that direction works, we’ll convert the agreed numbers into final legal-friendly terms.

Best —
Olga
